text:
sam: customer reports 401 invalid_api_key right after rotating a key. new key works from curl but their backend still gets 401

sam: request_id=01FZ2A9Q ; can reproduce in our logs as invalid_api_key for that req id

alex: can you paste the sanitized headers their service is sending (redact token)?

morgan: they mentioned a middleware that sets an X-Key-ID header for routing. might be a mismatch between that header and the token id.

sam: sanitized headers they sent:
```
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>
X-Key-ID: key_ABC123
User-Agent: acme-service/2.1
```

auth-bot: [auth] req=01FZ2A9Q reason=invalid_api_key detail=key_id_mismatch expected=key_DEF456 provided=key_ABC123

alex: looks like our auth layer compares the token prefix (key_DEF456) to any explicit X-Key-ID to prevent token/key impersonation. if a proxy injects a stale X-Key-ID you get 401 invalid_api_key.

morgan: I asked the customer to check their edge. they have an old nginx config that preserved a cached header from previous tokens. asked them to remove proxy_set_header X-Key-ID or rewrite it from the current Authorization value.

sam: they removed the header and retried — same request_id now shows 200 from their service. confirmed fix.

alex: suggest we add a short KB note: "401 after rotation caused by mismatched X-Key-ID header inserted by proxies" with example log line and mitigation (remove proxy_set_header / rewrite from Authorization).

morgan: I'll open a docs PR with reproduction and nginx snippet.

sam: marking resolved on our side, following up with ACME to confirm long-term. :thumbsup:
